liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Rub** (1 review): Described as a very hot audience-recorded version, after which the whole show picks up [3]
- **Loser** (1 review): Loser comes across with solid, heavy bass in the audience recording [3]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Morning Dew sounds fairly decent on the audience recording [9]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Runs almost 17 minutes, with Pigpen letting the band go wild [6]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Uncle John's Band is noted as being played electric in this performance [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Rub**: rare: 12 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd71-05-30.aud.miller.31968.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 119 min; rated 2/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording improves greatly after Bertha, though some sound problems return near the end of the show; Audience tape sound is poor, and becomes basically unlistenable somewhere during Lovelight [3][5]
- **gd1971-05-30.sbd.miller.94119.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 77 min; rated 4.29/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: The soundboard reel fades in during I Know You Rider, so earlier material is missing; Soundboard is upfront with a great mix; Cumberland Blues and Big Boss Man sound especially good; Described as a hi-fi stereo soundboard with an excellent mix, starting with I Know You Rider [2][4][6][7][14]

## Around the show

- Crowd was about half the size of the previous night's, many having been busted or hospitalized after that night [8]
- Reviewer says the band played as its original five-man lineup; remembers it as the last time Winterland could be walked into freely [8]
- Mentions the infamous Winterland acid dosing, which made headlines and pushed Bill Graham to reconsider his position [10]
- Many attendees were likely still drifting from the previous night's punch episode [14]
- Reviewer had only known this show from a brutal audience tape before hearing this soundboard portion [4]
- Claims the first part of this tape is really the first set from 5-28-71; only Deal onward is from 5-30 [10]
- After this show the band had weeks off before a France show, and worked up Sugaree, Brown-Eyed Women and Mr. Charlie [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-05-30.aud.miller.31968.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Audience: Unknown Mics [1]. Also: Transferred and edited by Charlie Miller from a DAT supplied by Jim Powell; Most of set II was released on 180-gram vinyl for Record Store Day; the audience tape fills in the rest [1][9]
- **gd1971-05-30.sbd.miller.94119.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel [2]
